parsed.rationale: Both `NowPlayingItem` (package `AppServices`, `Shared/AppServices/Sources/AppServices/NowPlayingService.swift:23`) and `PlaycutSelection` (package `app:iOS`, `WXYC/iOS/Views/Playlist/PlaylistView.swift:23`) are `type-alias-object` records sharing two fields — `playcut:Playcut` and an artwork field — but the artwork type diverges: `artwork:Image?` in `NowPlayingItem` versus `artwork:UIImage?` in `PlaycutSelection`. This divergence is precisely the structural signal for a PAT: the shared shape can be expressed as a protocol with an `associatedtype ArtworkImage` covering the platform-specific image type, while `playcut:Playcut` becomes a required concrete member. Neither record carries any restraint flag (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` are all false), so no intentional-duplication override applies. Introducing `PlaycutPresenting` in the `AppServices` package (already upstream of `app:iOS`) lets both the service layer and the UI layer conform with their respective image types without coupling `AppServices` to UIKit.
